New 'A setting that the file does not name keeps its default.  A marker still wins over the file, as which place wins says.'  Same rule, 'not' kept
Words unchanged: the See: line of the errors moved up inside its section, to close the opening above the first h3, so that it is the errors of the whole file and not of the last h3

The exceptions to 'a JSON string' are a list of four lines, one for each type; SQLSRC018, with 'null among them', is a bullet of its own.  Checked against SettingsFileKeys.TypeOf and schemas/settings-v1.schema.json: root boolean, generatorParameters array of strings, typeOverrides and libraryTypes objects of strings, columnTypes strings or objects of type and json
Two bullets: how a string is read, with SqlSource as the actor; and an empty or white-space string, which sets nothing and is no error, with the advice to leave the key out
Its lead-in states the rule; the URL, a code span, kept letter for letter
The h3 'Which settings files apply to a `.sql` file', from the bold lead-in 'The settings files of a `.sql` file', under phase 7's anchor files-of-a-sql-file; no <a id> added

One paragraph of 164 words is an opening of two sentences and six bullets: nearest wins; the three lists and generatorParameters add up, with both links; root true is the last; where to put it; root false; a file that is not JSON (SQLSRC015) gives nothing.  Checker: `"root": true` 5 > 6, as the advice to put the file is its own bullet and names it
Each lead-in now holds its whole rule; 'not those of the project's folder' and 'is not read, and applies to nothing' kept
The h3 'Which settings files the build checks', from the bold lead-in 'Which files are checked.', under phase 7's anchor which-files-are-checked; no <a id> added

Old text of site/settings.md:1047 as phase 7 corrected it (C-01, phase-07 row site/settings.md:1047): one paragraph of ten sentences and 310 words is an opening of three sentences and nine bullets, one rule each.  The words 'which only the tool checks' are kept, checked against SettingsFileSide.Reports (the build reports every setting but database, the tool dialect, output and database), SettingsFileTests.Run_InvalidDatabase_IsNotReported and MethodPlanner.DatabaseOf (the build reads database but does not check it).  The exception for a build through a symbolic link, and its link to #limit-symbolic-link, kept; the build folders and the NuGet folders checked against SqlSource.targets, SqlSourceFindBuildFolders.  Checker, sentences with no partner: old 'The build reads each settings file that the search ... reaches, whether or not a type claims that `.sql` file, and reports each mistake ...'; new 'It reads the file whether or not a type claims that `.sql` file.', 'not' kept.  Old 'Nor do the C# files that a NuGet package adds ... is not read on their account.'; new 'The C# files that a NuGet package adds to your project reach no settings file.' and 'So the build does not read a broken `sqlsource.json` above that folder ... because of these files.'  Same rules.  'unless' kept in the bullet of your own files
The h3 'Settings files in the build', from the bold lead-in 'In the build', under phase 7's anchor settings-file-in-the-build; no <a id> added

Old text of site/settings.md:1049 as phase 7 corrected it (C-02, phase-07 row site/settings.md:1049): an opening and five bullets; the two ways round a copy rule are a list.  'The project file holds no key of a settings file: an MSBuild property or item metadata named after one is not read' kept word for word as a lead-in, and 'nothing reports it' as 'Nothing reports such a property or metadata'

Its last sentence, the list of the five MSBuild properties a project sets, each with what it does, is cut to 'SqlSource has five MSBuild properties that a project sets' and a link to the table.  The table holds all five (SqlSourceIncludeFiles, SqlSourceOnline, SqlSourceEnvFile, SqlSourcePublicExceptions, SqlSourceRepositoryInterfaces), each with what it sets, and so do SqlSource.props 27, 45, 47 and SqlSource.targets 384, 394.  Its five links (msbuild.md#included-files, exceptions.md#public-exceptions, msbuild.md#online-build, msbuild.md#setting-env-file, repositories.md#repository-interfaces) went with the sentence; the table links each.  Checker: `SqlSourceIncludeFiles`, `SqlSourcePublicExceptions`, `SqlSourceOnline`, `SqlSourceEnvFile`, `SqlSourceRepositoryInterfaces` and `.env` 1 > 0, and `sqlsource` 2 > 1 (the `sqlsource` tool, of SqlSourceOnline's clause), all in that list
Unchanged: the h2 Limits, phase 7's new text
Unchanged: the heading of the limit, phase 7's new text (guide section 4: a limit's heading is not reworded)

The bullet is the three parts of a limit.  'What you see': the lead-in and the example, with each case a bullet; SQLSRC209, SQLSRC004 and SQLSRC005 stay with their cases.  'What to do': the two ways round it, a list.  Checker, sentences with no partner: old 'One in a folder above the link applies only when that folder is also above ...'; new 'A settings file in a folder above the link applies only if that folder is also above the folder the link leads to.', 'only' kept.  Old 'A `.sql` or C# file that your project lists by its full path ... and such a `.sql` file is not found by its type ...'; new, in three bullets, 'It gets none of those in `~/code` or below it.' and 'the type does not find such a `.sql` file', 'not' kept as 'none' and 'does not'

The two sentences of 'Why.', which the form of a limit asks for (guide section 4): a folder reached through a link has two paths, and the build does not always match a file by one with a settings file by the other.  Source: the comment of SqlSourceFindSettingsFiles in SqlSource.targets (the compiler resolves a link in a path, MSBuild keeps it)
